newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $62, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $62, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle near midday Monday were not trading, as bids at $62.00 per cwt were passed by owners pricing cattle from $64.00 to $65.00, feedlot sources said.
Fed cattle last sold at $63.00 late last week in light volume as packers and cattle owners settled into a standoff, the sources said.

Feedlots remain current in their marketings, with weights still running below a year ago. Average weights for the week ended Saturday were pegged at 1,164 lbs, compared with 1,166 estimated previous week and actual 1,182 last year, USDA said.
Showlists were expected larger than last week because of carryover of cattle held back by owners who resisted packer bids and trades at $63.00, sources said.
Because of the light weights, the carryover was not expected to burden the market unless demand stalls, they said.
Beef trade at midday Monday was light, with prices quoted down $0.06 to up $0.26 per cwt, USDA said. There were 50 fabricated loads of beef sold.
